title: Record Post-Hoc Irreversibility When Outcomes Break Expectations
decision: Add outcome semantics and post-hoc irreversibility flags to Decision Records to capture when reality breaks expected reversibility.
context: Reversibility is an expectation at decision time. In practice, decisions can become irreversible due to downstream effects (trust, contracts, regulations, public commitments).
rationale: Without post-hoc capture, organizations repeat the same category error: treating costly-to-undo outcomes as if they were reversible.
consequences: DMP can preserve classification drift and real-world constraints, improving future decision quality without rewriting history.
outcome_notes: The decision appeared reversible, but downstream dependencies and public commitments made rollback infeasible without major loss of trust.
scp_risk_notes: Observed irreversibility and trust-loss signals require explicit SCP-aware review.
alternatives: Treat reversibility as a one-time classification with no outcome tracking
Require supersession for every outcome update
